Application of Derivatives — JEE Main revision guide

The derivative tells how fast an output changes. On a graph it tells the slope. That one idea helps us find rising parts, falling parts, best values, and rates in changing shapes.

Study priority: derivative sign tables; local versus absolute best values; constraints and domains in optimization; rates with units; parameter conditions for increase. These priorities are teaching judgments, not measured formula-frequency ranks.

Source and syllabus details before studying

Current official Mathematics Unit 7 names rate of change, increasing/decreasing functions, and maxima/minima. The source also asks tangents/normals, differentials, inflection points and Rolle's theorem. We retain and teach every supplied question. Those extra tools are labelled supporting source extensions rather than separately named current-syllabus topics.

No answer-key error was found in these 353535 questions. Watch three wording details: a value is f(x)f(x)f(x), not its input xxx; a downward speed is positive though the height rate is negative; and an approximation is not an exact finite change.

Concept C01 — What the derivative actually measures

Think of a walk. Time is the input; distance travelled is the output. “Two metres each second” compares output change with input change. For a graph y=f(x)y=f(x)y=f(x), a small step hhh gives average slope

f(x+h)−f(x)h.\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}h.hf(x+h)−f(x)​.

Shrink the step towards zero:

f′(x)=lim⁡h→0f(x+h)−f(x)h.f'(x)=\lim_{h\to0}\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}h.f′(x)=h→0lim​hf(x+h)−f(x)​.

This is the instantaneous rate and the tangent slope. It is a number at one input, and a function when the input can vary.

  • f′(x)>0f'(x)>0f′(x)>0: a small move to the right raises the graph.
  • f′(x)<0f'(x)<0f′(x)<0: a small move to the right lowers it.
  • f′(x)=0f'(x)=0f′(x)=0: the tangent is horizontal. We still need to check whether the graph turns.

Quick derivative toolbox — Important for JEE Main. Use radians for trig derivatives.

(xn)′=nxn−1,(ex)′=ex,(ln⁡x)′=1x (x>0),(sin⁡x)′=cos⁡x,(cos⁡x)′=−sin⁡x,(tan⁡x)′=sec⁡2x,(uv)′=u′v+uv′,(uv)′=u′v−uv′v2 (v≠0),[F(g(x))]′=F′(g(x))g′(x).\begin{gathered} (x^n)'=nx^{n-1},\quad (e^x)'=e^x,\quad (\ln x)'=\frac1x\ (x>0),\\ (\sin x)'=\cos x,\quad(\cos x)'=-\sin x,\quad (\tan x)'=\sec^2x,\\ (uv)'=u'v+uv',\qquad \left(\frac uv\right)'=\frac{u'v-uv'}{v^2}\ (v\ne0),\\ [F(g(x))]'=F'(g(x))g'(x). \end{gathered}(xn)′=nxn−1,(ex)′=ex,(lnx)′=x1​ (x>0),(sinx)′=cosx,(cosx)′=−sinx,(tanx)′=sec2x,(uv)′=u′v+uv′,(vu​)′=v2u′v−uv′​ (v=0),[F(g(x))]′=F′(g(x))g′(x).​

The last rule says: outer change multiplied by inner change. For V(r(t))V(r(t))V(r(t)), it becomes dV/dt=(dV/dr)(dr/dt)dV/dt=(dV/dr)(dr/dt)dV/dt=(dV/dr)(dr/dt). Do not drop the second factor.

If position is s(t)s(t)s(t), velocity v=ds/dtv=ds/dtv=ds/dt and acceleration a=dv/dta=dv/dta=dv/dt. Speed is ∣v∣|v|∣v∣. For v≠0v\ne0v=0, speed rises when va>0va>0va>0 and falls when va<0va<0va<0: velocity and acceleration in the same direction increase speed. This connects the maths rate to a physical meaning.

Concept C02 — Tangent, normal and contact

Supporting source extension. A tangent is the straight line with the curve's slope at the chosen point. It can cross the curve elsewhere. A normal is the line at right angles to that tangent.

At P(x0,y0)P(x_0,y_0)P(x0​,y0​) on y=f(x)y=f(x)y=f(x) with finite slope m=f′(x0)m=f'(x_0)m=f′(x0​):

y−y0=m(x−x0)tangent.\boxed{y-y_0=m(x-x_0)}\quad\text{tangent}.y−y0​=m(x−x0​)​tangent.

For m≠0m\ne0m=0:

y−y0=−1m(x−x0)normal.\boxed{y-y_0=-\frac1m(x-x_0)}\quad\text{normal}.y−y0​=−m1​(x−x0​)​normal.

Why the minus reciprocal? Direction vectors (1,m)(1,m)(1,m) and (m,−1)(m,-1)(m,−1) have dot product m−m=0m-m=0m−m=0. They are perpendicular. If m=0m=0m=0, the normal is vertical, x=x0x=x_0x=x0​; do not divide by zero. A vertical tangent, where established, has a horizontal normal.

For an implicit curve F(x,y)=0F(x,y)=0F(x,y)=0, differentiate both sides while treating yyy as depending on xxx. Example: y2=4xy^2=4xy2=4x gives 2yy′=42yy'=42yy′=4, so y′=2/yy'=2/yy′=2/y when y≠0y\ne0y=0.

Concept C03 — Increasing and decreasing: read the derivative sign

On an interval, strictly increasing means

x1<x2⇒f(x1)<f(x2).x_1<x_2\quad\Rightarrow\quad f(x_1)<f(x_2).x1​<x2​⇒f(x1​)<f(x2​).

“Nondecreasing” allows equality. Important for JEE Main: if f′>0f'>0f′>0 throughout an interval, fff is strictly increasing there; if f′<0f'<0f′<0, it is strictly decreasing. If f′≥0f'\ge0f′≥0, it is nondecreasing. It is also strictly increasing if it is not constant on any subinterval, as for a polynomial with only isolated zero derivatives.

For example, x3x^3x3 is strictly increasing even though f′(0)=0f'(0)=0f′(0)=0. So “strictly increasing requires f′>0f'>0f′>0 at every point” is false.

Build a sign table in this order.

  1. Find the real domain. A missing input splits the domain.
  2. Factor f′f'f′. Mark its zeros and points where the derivative fails.
  3. Test the sign in each interval. Factors like exe^xex or a nonzero square keep a fixed sign.
  4. Translate +++ into rise and −-− into fall.

For f′=3(x−1)(x−3)f'=3(x-1)(x-3)f′=3(x−1)(x−3):

Input interval x−1x-1x−1 x−3x-3x−3 f′f'f′ Graph
x<1x<1x<1 −-− −-− +++ rises
1<x<31<x<31<x<3 +++ −-− −-− falls
x>3x>3x>3 +++ +++ +++ rises

When an option writes two open intervals joined by ∪\cup∪, read it in the usual exam sense: increasing on each listed interval. Do not compare an arbitrary point from one disconnected piece with a point from the other. Isolated stationary endpoints can often be included in a maximal interval, but the source options use the standard open derivative-sign intervals.

For a parameter question, “increasing for all real xxx” means the derivative cannot become negative anywhere. If f′=Ax2+Bx+Cf'=Ax^2+Bx+Cf′=Ax2+Bx+C and A>0A>0A>0:

f′(x)≥0 ∀x⟺B2−4AC≤0.f'(x)\ge0\ \forall x\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad B^2-4AC\le0.f′(x)≥0 ∀x⟺B2−4AC≤0.

Why? A positive-opening quadratic has its least height at the vertex; discriminant ≤0\le0≤0 keeps it on or above the axis. Check equality cases rather than discarding them automatically.

Concept C04 — A local maximum or minimum is a nearby comparison

A local maximum at ccc means f(c)f(c)f(c) is at least as high as all sufficiently nearby values. A local minimum is at least as low. “Local” means near that point; it need not win over the full domain.

Important for JEE Main: first-derivative sign test

Sign of f′ from left to rightWhat happens+ → −local maximum− → +local minimum+ → + or − → −no turn\begin{array}{c|c} \text{Sign of }f'\text{ from left to right}&\text{What happens}\\ \hline +\ \to\ -&\text{local maximum}\\ -\ \to\ +&\text{local minimum}\\ +\ \to\ +\text{ or }-\ \to\ -&\text{no turn} \end{array}Sign of f′ from left to right+ → −− → ++ → + or − → −​What happenslocal maximumlocal minimumno turn​​

The first row means “positive before, negative after”.

Candidate points are interior inputs where f′=0f'=0f′=0 or f′f'f′ does not exist but fff does. A differentiable interior extremum must satisfy f′=0f'=0f′=0. The reverse need not hold: x3x^3x3 crosses through zero with a horizontal tangent.

The second-derivative test is quicker when it decides the question:

f′(c)=0,{f′′(c)<0⇒local maximum,f′′(c)>0⇒local minimum,f′′(c)=0⇒test gives no decision.f'(c)=0,\quad \begin{cases} f''(c)<0&\Rightarrow\text{local maximum},\\ f''(c)>0&\Rightarrow\text{local minimum},\\ f''(c)=0&\Rightarrow\text{test gives no decision}. \end{cases}f′(c)=0,⎩⎨⎧​f′′(c)<0f′′(c)>0f′′(c)=0​⇒local maximum,⇒local minimum,⇒test gives no decision.​

At zero, x4x^4x4 has a minimum, −x4-x^4−x4 a maximum, and x3x^3x3 neither. All have f′′(0)=0f''(0)=0f′′(0)=0. Go back to signs or direct value comparison.

Concept C05 — Absolute best values need the whole allowed domain

An absolute maximum is the greatest attained value in the full allowed domain; an absolute minimum is the least. Important for JEE Main: for a continuous function on a closed bounded interval [a,b][a,b][a,b], both exist.

Make a small table of f(a)f(a)f(a), f(b)f(b)f(b) and f(c)f(c)f(c) at every interior critical point. Compare the values. Endpoints can win even when their derivative is nonzero.

On an open or unbounded interval, existence needs checking. For x>0x>0x>0, f(x)=xf(x)=xf(x)=x has no minimum: values approach 000, but x=0x=0x=0 is not allowed. The infimum, the greatest lower bound, is 000. It is not an attained minimum.

For xln⁡xx\ln xxlnx on x>0x>0x>0, the derivative changes from negative to positive at 1/e1/e1/e. Every allowed input on the left decreases towards that point, and every input on the right increases away. This proves a global minimum despite the open domain.

Concept C06 — Related rates: first connect the changing quantities

Important for JEE Main. “Rate” means change per unit time. Draw the shape, name its changing lengths, write a true relation, then differentiate with respect to time. Insert the current measurements afterwards.

For a sphere:

V=43πr3,dVdt=4πr2drdt.V=\frac43\pi r^3,\qquad \frac{dV}{dt}=4\pi r^2\frac{dr}{dt}.V=34​πr3,dtdV​=4πr2dtdr​.

dV/dtdV/dtdV/dt has units volume/time; dr/dtdr/dtdr/dt has units length/time. The surface area 4πr24\pi r^24πr2 converts one rate into the other.

For a fixed ladder of length LLL, foot distance xxx and top height yyy:

x2+y2=L2⇒xdxdt+ydydt=0.x^2+y^2=L^2 \quad\Rightarrow\quad x\frac{dx}{dt}+y\frac{dy}{dt}=0.x2+y2=L2⇒xdtdx​+ydtdy​=0.

If dx/dt>0dx/dt>0dx/dt>0, then dy/dt<0dy/dt<0dy/dt<0: moving the foot out lowers the top. If you put x=3x=3x=3 before differentiating, you turn a changing quantity into a constant and lose its rate.

Other useful shape relations:

Scube=6a2,Vcube=a3,Acircle=πr2,Vcone=13πr2h.S_{\rm cube}=6a^2,\quad V_{\rm cube}=a^3,\quad A_{\rm circle}=\pi r^2,\quad V_{\rm cone}=\frac13\pi r^2h.Scube​=6a2,Vcube​=a3,Acircle​=πr2,Vcone​=31​πr2h.

For water in a conical tank, first use similar triangles to relate rrr to hhh. If r/h=R/Hr/h=R/Hr/h=R/H, substitute r=(R/H)hr=(R/H)hr=(R/H)h so volume depends on one changing length. Do not hold rrr fixed when the surface radius also grows.

Concept C07 — A tangent gives a nearby estimate

Supporting source extension. For a small input change Δx\Delta xΔx, the tangent predicts

Δy=f(a+Δx)−f(a)≈f′(a)Δx.\Delta y=f(a+\Delta x)-f(a)\approx f'(a)\Delta x.Δy=f(a+Δx)−f(a)≈f′(a)Δx.

The differential is dy=f′(a) dxdy=f'(a)\,dxdy=f′(a)dx; set dx=Δxdx=\Delta xdx=Δx for the estimate. Thus

f(a+Δx)≈f(a)+f′(a)Δx.\boxed{f(a+\Delta x)\approx f(a)+f'(a)\Delta x}.f(a+Δx)≈f(a)+f′(a)Δx​.

Take 25.2\sqrt{25.2}25.2​. Choose a=25a=25a=25, because 25=5\sqrt{25}=525​=5 is easy. The input grows by 0.20.20.2, not by 25.225.225.2. The slope is 1/(225)=1/101/(2\sqrt{25})=1/101/(225​)=1/10. The predicted output grows by 0.020.020.02.

For y=Cxny=Cx^ny=Cxn with positive measured xxx and nonzero yyy:

dyy=ndxx.\frac{dy}{y}=n\frac{dx}{x}.ydy​=nxdx​.

Multiply by 100100100 for approximate percentage change. For a volume proportional to r3r^3r3, a small 0.1%0.1\%0.1% radius error gives about 0.3%0.3\%0.3% volume error. For an error bound use absolute values. This ignores terms in (Δx)2(\Delta x)^2(Δx)2 and higher; it is not an exact formula for a large error.

Concept C08 — Before differentiating, look for a useful inequality

Important for JEE Main — AM–GM. For positive numbers u,vu,vu,v,

u+v≥2uv,u+v\ge2\sqrt{uv},u+v≥2uv​,

with equality when u=vu=vu=v. It comes from (u−v)2≥0(\sqrt u-\sqrt v)^2\ge0(u​−v​)2≥0. For nnn positive terms, their sum is at least nnn times their product's nnnth root; equality needs all terms equal.

Did you notice the reciprocal pair in ax+b/xax+b/xax+b/x, with a,b,x>0a,b,x>0a,b,x>0? Their product is the fixed number ababab. Therefore

ax+bx≥2ab,x=ba at equality.\boxed{ax+\frac bx\ge2\sqrt{ab}},\qquad x=\sqrt{\frac ba}\text{ at equality}.ax+xb​≥2ab​​,x=ab​​ at equality.

Checking equality is essential: a bound is the minimum only if some allowed input reaches it. For 2x+1/x22x+1/x^22x+1/x2, split 2x2x2x as x+xx+xx+x; now the three-term product is 111. This is a purposeful expansion.

Important for JEE Main — Cauchy–Schwarz inequality. For real numbers,

(u1v1+⋯+unvn)2≤(u12+⋯+un2)(v12+⋯+vn2).(u_1v_1+\cdots+u_nv_n)^2 \le(u_1^2+\cdots+u_n^2)(v_1^2+\cdots+v_n^2).(u1​v1​+⋯+un​vn​)2≤(u12​+⋯+un2​)(v12​+⋯+vn2​).

Meaning: the dot product of two lists cannot be larger in magnitude than the product of their lengths. Equality needs proportional lists, including the usual zero-vector case.

For two terms this is just a square:

(u2+v2)(a2+b2)−(au+bv)2=(bu−av)2≥0.(u^2+v^2)(a^2+b^2)-(au+bv)^2=(bu-av)^2\ge0.(u2+v2)(a2+b2)−(au+bv)2=(bu−av)2≥0.

Set (u,v)=(sin⁡x,cos⁡x)(u,v)=(\sin x,\cos x)(u,v)=(sinx,cosx) and (a,b)=(1,1)(a,b)=(1,1)(a,b)=(1,1):

∣sin⁡x+cos⁡x∣≤1⋅2=2.|\sin x+\cos x|\le\sqrt{1\cdot2}=\sqrt2.∣sinx+cosx∣≤1⋅2​=2​.

For the maximum +2+\sqrt2+2​, equality needs sin⁡x=cos⁡x=1/2\sin x=\cos x=1/\sqrt2sinx=cosx=1/2​. A negative equal pair gives the minimum −2-\sqrt2−2​.

Another possible approach — change the view to a wave:

Asin⁡x+Bcos⁡x=Rsin⁡(x+ϕ),R=A2+B2,A\sin x+B\cos x=R\sin(x+\phi),\quad R=\sqrt{A^2+B^2},Asinx+Bcosx=Rsin(x+ϕ),R=A2+B2​,

where Rcos⁡ϕ=AR\cos\phi=ARcosϕ=A, Rsin⁡ϕ=BR\sin\phi=BRsinϕ=B. Over all real inputs its range is [−R,R][-R,R][−R,R]. On a restricted interval, the peak phase may be outside the interval: check that and the endpoints. This shortcut does not automatically solve every restricted trig maximum.

Concept C09 — Bending and inflection

Supporting source extension. f′f'f′ measures slope. f′′f''f′′ measures how that slope changes as we move right.

  • f′′>0f''>0f′′>0: slopes increase; the graph bends like a bowl, called concave up.
  • f′′<0f''<0f′′<0: slopes decrease; it bends like an upside-down bowl, called concave down.
  • An inflection point is a continuous point where the bending changes from one type to the other.

Solve f′′=0f''=0f′′=0 to get candidates, then check the signs on both sides. At x=0x=0x=0, x4x^4x4 has f′′=12x2≥0f''=12x^2\ge0f′′=12x2≥0 on both sides, so it has no inflection there. For functions whose second derivative fails to exist, such points can also be candidates; the definition is change of bending, not just f′′=0f''=0f′′=0.

Concept C10 — Optimization: translate the words into one variable

Important for JEE Main. An optimization problem asks for the best possible value under given restrictions. Use this order:

  1. Draw and name the lengths or quantities. State what must be positive.
  2. Write the target: volume, area, distance, product or cost.
  3. Use the constraint to remove one variable.
  4. Find candidates and prove which is best on the actual domain.
  5. Return to the requested quantity, with units.

Distance clue. Square roots make differentiation longer. Since s\sqrt ss​ is increasing for s≥0s\ge0s≥0, minimizing distance DDD is equivalent to minimizing D2D^2D2. Do not square a signed expression and assume its order is preserved.

For P(3,0)P(3,0)P(3,0) and Q(x,y)Q(x,y)Q(x,y) on y2=4xy^2=4xy2=4x:

D2=(x−3)2+y2=(x−3)2+4x=(x−1)2+8,x≥0.D^2=(x-3)^2+y^2 =(x-3)^2+4x=(x-1)^2+8,\qquad x\ge0.D2=(x−3)2+y2=(x−3)2+4x=(x−1)2+8,x≥0.

The nonnegative square shows the minimum directly. Both y=2y=2y=2 and y=−2y=-2y=−2 are possible at x=1x=1x=1.

Constraint clue. For x+y=Lx+y=Lx+y=L and x,y>0x,y>0x,y>0, rewrite xpyqx^py^qxpyq as xp(L−x)qx^p(L-x)^qxp(L−x)q, with 0<x<L0<x<L0<x<L. For p,q>0p,q>0p,q>0,

ddxln⁡[xp(L−x)q]=px−qL−x=0⇒x:y=p:q.\frac d{dx}\ln[x^p(L-x)^q]=\frac px-\frac q{L-x}=0 \quad\Rightarrow\quad x:y=p:q.dxd​ln[xp(L−x)q]=xp​−L−xq​=0⇒x:y=p:q.

The derivative changes from positive to negative there; endpoint limits are zero. Thus it is the global maximum. This is why a repeated factor x2yx^2yx2y does not usually peak at x=yx=yx=y.

Concept C11 — Use graph shape to count roots or impose contact

Important for JEE Main. Roots are places where the graph meets the horizontal axis. A derivative sign table tells where there can be at most one root on each rising or falling interval.

For g(x)=x3−3x+kg(x)=x^3-3x+kg(x)=x3−3x+k, the turns are fixed at x=−1x=-1x=−1 and x=1x=1x=1; changing kkk shifts the whole graph up or down.

g(−1)=k+2,g(1)=k−2.g(-1)=k+2,\qquad g(1)=k-2.g(−1)=k+2,g(1)=k−2.

There are three distinct real roots exactly when the local high point is above the axis and the local low point below it:

k+2>0,k−2<0⟺−2<k<2.k+2>0,\quad k-2<0 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad -2<k<2.k+2>0,k−2<0⟺−2<k<2.

At equality, a turn sits on the axis, giving a repeated root rather than three distinct roots. Do not replace the strict inequalities by weak ones.

For a line touching a quadratic graph, the difference of their yyy expressions is a quadratic with a double zero. For a general curve, “same point and same slope” is the basic test; a quadratic discriminant trick applies only after the intersection equation really is quadratic.

Concept C12 — Equal endpoints and bounded slopes

Rolle's theorem — supporting source extension. A function continuous on [a,b][a,b][a,b], differentiable on (a,b)(a,b)(a,b), with f(a)=f(b)f(a)=f(b)f(a)=f(b) has at least one interior ccc with f′(c)=0f'(c)=0f′(c)=0.

Picture a smooth journey starting and finishing at the same height. Somewhere the tangent is horizontal. The theorem promises existence; solve f′=0f'=0f′=0 and keep only roots inside (a,b)(a,b)(a,b). A corner can break the differentiability condition.

The mean value theorem, also a supporting extension, says under the same continuity/differentiability conditions:

f′(c)=f(b)−f(a)b−af'(c)=\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}f′(c)=b−af(b)−f(a)​

for some interior ccc. The right side is the chord's average slope.

Bounded-slope questions can also use ordinary monotonicity. If f′≤Mf'\le Mf′≤M, define g(x)=f(x)−Mxg(x)=f(x)-Mxg(x)=f(x)−Mx. Then g′≤0g'\le0g′≤0, so for b>ab>ab>a,

f(b)−Mb≤f(a)−Ma⇒f(b)−f(a)≤M(b−a).f(b)-Mb\le f(a)-Ma \quad\Rightarrow\quad \boxed{f(b)-f(a)\le M(b-a)}.f(b)−Mb≤f(a)−Ma⇒f(b)−f(a)≤M(b−a)​.

If ∣f′∣≤M|f'|\le M∣f′∣≤M, then ∣f(b)−f(a)∣≤M∣b−a∣|f(b)-f(a)|\le M|b-a|∣f(b)−f(a)∣≤M∣b−a∣. A derivative bound controls total rise even when we do not know the exact function. To claim a largest possible value, also give a function that reaches the bound.

Worked solutions to the 35 PDF questions

Read the question first. Notice the pattern, choose a route, then calculate. Alternative methods below are fully visible.

Question 1 — The derivative gives the tangent slope

PDF page 54 | MCQ | Notes: C01,C02

The equation of the tangent to the curve y=x3−3x+2y=x^3-3x+2y=x3−3x+2 at the point where x=2x=2x=2 is

  • (a) y=9x+14y=9x+14y=9x+14
  • (b) y=3x−2y=3x-2y=3x−2
  • (c) y=9x−14y=9x-14y=9x−14
  • (d) y=9x−4y=9x-4y=9x−4

We need a point and a slope. At x=2x=2x=2, the curve's height is 8−6+2=48-6+2=48−6+2=4. So the tangent must pass through (2,4)(2,4)(2,4).

y′=3x2−3,m=3(2)2−3=9.y'=3x^2-3,\quad m=3(2)^2-3=9.y′=3x2−3,m=3(2)2−3=9.

Put that point and slope into the line equation:

y−4=9(x−2)⇒y=9x−14(c).y-4=9(x-2)\quad\Rightarrow\quad \boxed{y=9x-14}\quad\text{(c)}.y−4=9(x−2)⇒y=9x−14​(c).

Check: at x=2x=2x=2 the line gives 444. Option (b) also passes through that point, but its slope is 333, so a point check alone cannot choose the tangent.

Question 2 — The normal is perpendicular to the tangent

PDF page 54 | MCQ | Notes: C02

The equation of the normal to the parabola y=x2y=x^2y=x2 at the point (1,1)(1,1)(1,1) is

  • (a) x+2y=3x+2y=3x+2y=3
  • (b) 2x+y=32x+y=32x+y=3
  • (c) x−2y=−1x-2y=-1x−2y=−1
  • (d) x+y=2x+y=2x+y=2

Normal means the line at right angles to the tangent. First find the tangent's slope, then turn it by a right angle.

y′=2x,mtangent=2,mnormal=−12.y'=2x,\qquad m_{\rm tangent}=2,\qquad m_{\rm normal}=-\frac12.y′=2x,mtangent​=2,mnormal​=−21​.

Thus

y−1=−12(x−1)⇒x+2y=3(a).y-1=-\frac12(x-1) \quad\Rightarrow\quad \boxed{x+2y=3}\quad\text{(a)}.y−1=−21​(x−1)⇒x+2y=3​(a).

Check: (1,1)(1,1)(1,1) satisfies the equation and 2(−1/2)=−12(-1/2)=-12(−1/2)=−1. Using slope 222 would find the tangent, a different line.

Question 3 — Parallel lines have the same slope

PDF page 54 | MCQ | Notes: C02

The tangent to y=x2+3xy=x^2+3xy=x2+3x is parallel to the line y=7x+1y=7x+1y=7x+1 at a point. The ordinate of that point is

  • (a) 444
  • (b) 777
  • (c) 141414
  • (d) 101010

Ordinate means the yyy coordinate. The given line has slope 777. Parallel tangents must also have slope 777.

y′=2x+3=7⇒x=2,y=22+3(2)=10(d).y'=2x+3=7\Rightarrow x=2,\qquad y=2^2+3(2)=\boxed{10}\quad\text{(d)}.y′=2x+3=7⇒x=2,y=22+3(2)=10​(d).

We used 7x+17x+17x+1 only to read the slope; the contact point is on the curve, so its height must come from x2+3xx^2+3xx2+3x.

Question 4 — Angle between curves means angle between their tangents

PDF page 54 | MCQ | Notes: C02

The acute angle between the curves y=x2y=x^2y=x2 and x=y2x=y^2x=y2 at their point of intersection (1,1)(1,1)(1,1) is

  • (a) tan⁡−143\tan^{-1}\dfrac43tan−134​
  • (b) tan⁡−134\tan^{-1}\dfrac34tan−143​
  • (c) π4\dfrac\pi44π​
  • (d) tan⁡−112\tan^{-1}\dfrac12tan−121​

The curves meet, but each has its own direction there. Draw their tangents at (1,1)(1,1)(1,1). The acute angle between those lines is the angle asked.

For y=x2y=x^2y=x2, m1=2x=2m_1=2x=2m1​=2x=2. For x=y2x=y^2x=y2, implicit differentiation gives

1=2y y′⇒m2=12y=12.1=2y\,y'\Rightarrow m_2=\frac1{2y}=\frac12.1=2yy′⇒m2​=2y1​=21​.

Therefore

tan⁡θ=∣m1−m21+m1m2∣=2−121+1=34,θ=tan⁡−1(3/4)(b).\tan\theta= \left|\frac{m_1-m_2}{1+m_1m_2}\right| =\frac{2-\tfrac12}{1+1}=\frac34, \qquad \boxed{\theta=\tan^{-1}(3/4)}\quad\text{(b)}.tanθ=​1+m1​m2​m1​−m2​​​=1+12−21​​=43​,θ=tan−1(3/4)​(b).

Another possible approach: tangent directions (1,2)(1,2)(1,2) and (2,1)(2,1)(2,1) have dot product 444, both lengths 5\sqrt55​. Thus cos⁡θ=4/5\cos\theta=4/5cosθ=4/5; the positive sine is 3/53/53/5, giving tan⁡θ=3/4\tan\theta=3/4tanθ=3/4 again.

Question 5 — Build a sign table from the derivative factors

PDF page 54 | MCQ | Notes: C03

The function f(x)=x3−6x2+9x+1f(x)=x^3-6x^2+9x+1f(x)=x3−6x2+9x+1 is strictly increasing in

  • (a) (1,3)(1,3)(1,3)
  • (b) (−∞,1)∪(3,∞)(-\infty,1)\cup(3,\infty)(−∞,1)∪(3,∞)
  • (c) (−∞,3)(-\infty,3)(−∞,3)
  • (d) (0,3)(0,3)(0,3)

Did you notice that the derivative factors into two easy sign-changing pieces?

f′(x)=3x2−12x+9=3(x−1)(x−3).f'(x)=3x^2-12x+9=3(x-1)(x-3).f′(x)=3x2−12x+9=3(x−1)(x−3).
Interval Signs of (x−1),(x−3)(x-1),(x-3)(x−1),(x−3) Sign of f′f'f′
(−∞,1)(-\infty,1)(−∞,1) −,−-,-−,− +++
(1,3)(1,3)(1,3) +,−+,-+,− −-−
(3,∞)(3,\infty)(3,∞) +,++,++,+ +++

So the listed increasing pieces are (−∞,1)∪(3,∞)\boxed{(-\infty,1)\cup(3,\infty)}(−∞,1)∪(3,∞)​, (b). This means increasing on each piece separately. It does not compare every input in the first piece with every input in the second.

Question 6 — An exponential factor never changes sign

PDF page 54 | MCQ | Notes: C03

The interval in which f(x)=x2e−xf(x)=x^2e^{-x}f(x)=x2e−x is strictly increasing is

  • (a) (−∞,0)(-\infty,0)(−∞,0)
  • (b) (2,∞)(2,\infty)(2,∞)
  • (c) (−∞,2)(-\infty,2)(−∞,2)
  • (d) (0,2)(0,2)(0,2)

Keep the positive factor out of the sign decision. Product differentiation gives

f′=2xe−x−x2e−x=e−xx(2−x).f'=2xe^{-x}-x^2e^{-x}=e^{-x}x(2-x).f′=2xe−x−x2e−x=e−xx(2−x).

Since e−x>0e^{-x}>0e−x>0, only x(2−x)x(2-x)x(2−x) matters:

x(−∞,0)(0,2)(2,∞)f′−+−\begin{array}{c|ccc} x&(-\infty,0)&(0,2)&(2,\infty)\\ \hline f'&-&+&- \end{array}xf′​(−∞,0)−​(0,2)+​(2,∞)−​​

Thus (0,2)\boxed{(0,2)}(0,2)​, (d). The exponential getting smaller does not by itself make the whole product smaller; x2x^2x2 changes too.

Question 7 — Find the maximum value after locating the turn

PDF page 54 | MCQ | Notes: C04

The local maximum value of f(x)=2x3−9x2+12x+5f(x)=2x^3-9x^2+12x+5f(x)=2x3−9x2+12x+5 is

  • (a) 101010
  • (b) 999
  • (c) 555
  • (d) 141414

A maximum value is a height, not an input. Find where the graph changes from rising to falling.

f′=6x2−18x+12=6(x−1)(x−2).f'=6x^2-18x+12=6(x-1)(x-2).f′=6x2−18x+12=6(x−1)(x−2).

The signs are +,−,++,-,++,−,+ on the three intervals. Hence x=1x=1x=1 gives the local maximum; x=2x=2x=2 gives the local minimum.

f(1)=2−9+12+5=10(a).f(1)=2-9+12+5=\boxed{10}\quad\text{(a)}.f(1)=2−9+12+5=10​(a).

Another possible approach: f′′=12x−18f''=12x-18f′′=12x−18 is negative at 111 and positive at 222. After finding the stationary inputs, this quickly classifies them.

Question 8 — Check the endpoints as well as stationary points

PDF page 54 | Numerical value | Notes: C05

If MMM and mmm are the absolute maximum and absolute minimum values of f(x)=x3−12xf(x)=x^3-12xf(x)=x3−12x on [−3,5][-3,5][−3,5], then M+m=M+m=M+m= ____.

Absolute means compare the whole allowed interval. Solving f′=0f'=0f′=0 alone could miss an endpoint winner.

f′=3x2−12=0⇒x=±2.f'=3x^2-12=0\Rightarrow x=\pm2.f′=3x2−12=0⇒x=±2.

Both lie inside [−3,5][-3,5][−3,5]. Compare:

Input −3-3−3 −2-2−2 222 555
f(x)=x3−12xf(x)=x^3-12xf(x)=x3−12x 999 161616 −16-16−16 656565

So M=65M=65M=65, m=−16m=-16m=−16, and M+m=49\boxed{M+m=49}M+m=49​. The derivative finds interior candidates; the closed interval adds the endpoints.

Question 9 — Volume rate and radius rate are different quantities

PDF page 54 | MCQ | Notes: C06

Gas is pumped into a spherical balloon at 10 cm3/s10\ \mathrm{cm^3/s}10 cm3/s. The rate at which the radius increases when r=5 cmr=5\ \mathrm{cm}r=5 cm is

  • (a) 1π cm/s\dfrac1\pi\ \mathrm{cm/s}π1​ cm/s
  • (b) 1100π cm/s\dfrac1{100\pi}\ \mathrm{cm/s}100π1​ cm/s
  • (c) 110π cm/s\dfrac1{10\pi}\ \mathrm{cm/s}10π1​ cm/s
  • (d) 14π cm/s\dfrac1{4\pi}\ \mathrm{cm/s}4π1​ cm/s

The input rate is volume per second; the wanted rate is radius per second. Connect them with the sphere's volume.

V=43πr3⇒dVdt=4πr2drdt.V=\frac43\pi r^3 \Rightarrow \frac{dV}{dt}=4\pi r^2\frac{dr}{dt}.V=34​πr3⇒dtdV​=4πr2dtdr​.

At the stated instant,

10=4π(5)2drdt⇒drdt=110π cm/s(c).10=4\pi(5)^2\frac{dr}{dt} \Rightarrow \boxed{\frac{dr}{dt}=\frac1{10\pi}\ \mathrm{cm/s}}\quad\text{(c)}.10=4π(5)2dtdr​⇒dtdr​=10π1​ cm/s​(c).

Unit check: (cm3/s)/cm2=cm/s(\mathrm{cm^3/s})/\mathrm{cm^2}=\mathrm{cm/s}(cm3/s)/cm2=cm/s. Do not set r=5r=5r=5 before differentiating; rrr is changing.

Question 10 — The ladder gives a relation between two changing lengths

PDF page 55 | Numerical value | Notes: C06

A ladder 5 m5\ \mathrm m5 m long rests against a wall. Its foot is pulled away from the wall at 2 m/s2\ \mathrm{m/s}2 m/s. The speed at which the top slides down when the foot is 3 m3\ \mathrm m3 m from the wall is ____ m/s\mathrm{m/s}m/s.

Name both changing lengths. Let xxx be the foot's distance from the wall and yyy the top's height. The fixed ladder is the right triangle's hypotenuse.

x2+y2=25,2xdxdt+2ydydt=0.x^2+y^2=25,\qquad 2x\frac{dx}{dt}+2y\frac{dy}{dt}=0.x2+y2=25,2xdtdx​+2ydtdy​=0.

When x=3x=3x=3, y=25−9=4y=\sqrt{25-9}=4y=25−9​=4. Hence

dydt=−xydxdt=−34(2)=−32 m/s.\frac{dy}{dt}=-\frac xy\frac{dx}{dt} =-\frac34(2)=-\frac32\ \mathrm{m/s}.dtdy​=−yx​dtdx​=−43​(2)=−23​ m/s.

The negative sign says the height decreases. The asked downward speed is its magnitude: 1.5 m/s\boxed{1.5\ \mathrm{m/s}}1.5 m/s​.

Using differentials, the approximate value of 25.2\sqrt{25.2}25.2​ is

f′(x)=12x,f′(25)=110,dy=110(0.2)=0.02.f'(x)=\frac1{2\sqrt x},\quad f'(25)=\frac1{10}, \quad dy=\frac1{10}(0.2)=0.02.f′(x)=2x​1​,f′(25)=101​,dy=101​(0.2)=0.02.

Question 12 — A horizontal tangent need not be a maximum or minimum

  • (c) Statement I is false but Statement II is true

Zero slope does not automatically mean a turn. For x3x^3x3, negative inputs give negative outputs and positive inputs give positive outputs. So f(0)=0f(0)=0f(0)=0 is neither a nearby highest nor a nearby lowest value.

Also f′=3x2>0f'=3x^2>0f′=3x2>0 on both sides of 000. It is zero only at 000, with no sign change. Both statements are true, option (a).

4x+9x≥236=12.4x+\frac9x\ge2\sqrt{36}=12.4x+x9​≥236​=12.

Question 15 — Write the box dimensions before maximizing volume

PDF page 55 | Numerical value | Notes: C10,C05

An open box is made by cutting equal squares of side xxx cm from the corners of a square tin sheet of side 181818 cm and folding up the sides. The maximum volume of the box is ____ cm3\mathrm{cm^3}cm3.

Draw the cuts before writing volume. Each side loses xxx at both ends, so the folded base is (18−2x)(18-2x)(18−2x) by (18−2x)(18-2x)(18−2x); the height is xxx.

V=x(18−2x)2,0<x<9.V=x(18-2x)^2,\qquad 0<x<9.V=x(18−2x)2,0<x<9.

V′=(18−2x)2−4x(18−2x)=(18−2x)(18−6x).V'=(18-2x)^2-4x(18-2x) =(18-2x)(18-6x).V′=(18−2x)2−4x(18−2x)=(18−2x)(18−6x).

The first factor is positive in the physical domain. The second changes +→−+\to-+→− at x=3x=3x=3. So that point gives the global maximum; the limiting volumes at 000 and 999 are zero.

Vmax⁡=3(18−6)2=432 cm3.V_{\max}=3(18-6)^2=\boxed{432\ \mathrm{cm^3}}.Vmax​=3(18−6)2=432 cm3​.

Question 16 — Minimize distance squared, with the curve constraint

PDF page 55 | MCQ | Notes: C10,C05

The shortest distance of the point (3,0)(3,0)(3,0) from the parabola y2=4xy^2=4xy2=4x is

  • (a) 222
  • (b) 5\sqrt55​
  • (c) 333
  • (d) 222\sqrt222​

A distance is a square root. We can first minimize its square. Squaring preserves the order of nonnegative distances.

Let Q(x,y)Q(x,y)Q(x,y) be a point on the parabola and P=(3,0)P=(3,0)P=(3,0).

D2=(x−3)2+y2.D^2=(x-3)^2+y^2.D2=(x−3)2+y2.

Question 17 — A cubic needs one turn above and the other below the axis

PDF page 55 | Numerical value | Notes: C11

The number of integer values of kkk for which x3−3x+k=0x^3-3x+k=0x3−3x+k=0 has three distinct real roots is ____.

Three distinct roots mean three separate axis crossings. The cubic rises, falls, then rises. Its middle high point must be above the axis and its middle low point below.

g′=3(x2−1),g(−1)=k+2,g(1)=k−2.g'=3(x^2-1),\qquad g(-1)=k+2,\quad g(1)=k-2.g′=3(x2−1),g(−1)=k+2,g(1)=k−2.

Thus k+2>0k+2>0k+2>0 and k−2<0k-2<0k−2<0, giving −2<k<2-2<k<2−2<k<2. The integers are −1,0,1-1,0,1−1,0,1, so the answer is 3\boxed33​.

Each outer branch runs to an opposite infinite end and is strictly increasing; the middle branch is strictly decreasing. The stated strict height inequalities therefore give exactly one root on each of the three pieces. At k=±2k=\pm2k=±2 two roots merge at a turn, so those endpoints are excluded.

Which of the following statements are correct?

(A) f(x)=x3−3xf(x)=x^3-3xf(x)=x3−3x has a local maximum at x=−1x=-1x=−1.

(B) f(x)=x3−3xf(x)=x^3-3xf(x)=x3−3x has a local minimum at x=1x=1x=1.

(C) f(x)=x4f(x)=x^4f(x)=x4 has a point of inflection at x=0x=0x=0.

(D) The absolute maximum of sin⁡x\sin xsinx on R\mathbb RR is 111.

  • (a) (A), (B) and (D) only
  • (b) (A), (B) and (C) only
  • (c) (B), (C) and (D) only
  • (d) (A) and (C) only

Use the correct test for each claim.

For x3−3xx^3-3xx3−3x, f′=3(x−1)(x+1)f'=3(x-1)(x+1)f′=3(x−1)(x+1) has signs +,−,++,-,++,−,+. Thus −1-1−1 is a local maximum and 111 a local minimum: A and B true.

For x4x^4x4, f′′=12x2f''=12x^2f′′=12x2 is positive on both sides of zero. There is no bending change: C false.

Finally sin⁡x≤1\sin x\le1sinx≤1 for every real xxx, and 111 is attained at π/2+2kπ\pi/2+2k\piπ/2+2kπ: D true.

Therefore A, B and D only\boxed{\text{A, B and D only}}A, B and D only​, (a).
